access.edition_or_version: Collected in The Death of the Moth and Other Essays (Hogarth Press, 1942, posthumous; collection imprint verified 2026-09-24); in copyright — describe only.

tone_mechanisms_observed: two-beat shape: sustained concrete watching first, then assessment — never the reverse order
abstraction ('life', 'death') enters only after the scene has earned it and stays tied to the single specimen
no thesis and no lesson: reflection ends where the observation ends
staccato present-tense observation flowing into longer meditative periods
mechanics.point_of_view: Close observer of a watched insect, widening to mortality, then returning to the particular — distance moves out and back rather than staying abstract.
mechanics.tense_and_structure: Present-tense watching drives the scene; reflective generalization shifts to a gnomic present that never detaches from the window, the pane, the day.
mechanics.rhythm_and_cadence: Short observation clauses alternating with longer meditative periods; the sentence expands exactly where the meditation deepens.
mechanics.psychic_distance: Near (the moth) to far (mortality) and back again — the oscillation itself keeps the reflection from preaching.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Sustained metaphor of the moth as combatant/actor; 'life' dramatized through one body rather than asserted.
mechanics.copyright_note: In copyright (1942). Described by technique only; no passage reproduced.
